portfolio.title: LLM Evaluation Portfolio
portfolio.description: An applied research and demonstration portfolio about structured, reproducible evaluation of large language model outputs.
portfolio.scope: This is a demonstration of evaluation framework design and stress testing, not a representative benchmark or production evaluation system.
portfolio.approach: Framework design, multi-dimensional rubrics, controlled stress tests, cross-case analysis, and methodology refinement.

pillar.name: Citation Verification
pillar.summary: Checks whether cited sources actually support specific AI-generated claims, separating source entailment from factual truth and source quality.

pillar.name: LLM Response Evaluation
pillar.summary: Evaluates cooperative responses across seven dimensions: factual accuracy, relevance, completeness, instruction following, reasoning quality, hallucination or unsupported claims, and clarity.
pillar.proposedRevision: Extends the critical failure override from two to all seven dimensions; this revision is proposed, not independently validated.

pillar.name: Adversarial Testing
pillar.summary: Tests resilience to prompt injection, ambiguity, false premises, constraint overload, leading questions, distracting context, conflicting requirements, and pressure for unwarranted certainty.

pillar.name: Methodology and Meta-Evaluation
pillar.summary: Explains the task-specific rubrics, scoring design, cross-framework comparison, limitations, and future validation work.

keyFindings.finding: High aggregate scores can hide complete failure on a critical dimension in the designed cases.
Response Evaluation v1 protected against factual inaccuracy and hallucination but not other severe usability failures, motivating the proposed v2 override.
Cooperative traits such as agreeableness and confidence can become vulnerabilities under adversarial prompts.

portfolio.limitations: Cases were deliberately designed to probe failure modes and do not estimate real-world failure rates. Proposed revisions need independent validation, and rubric judgments need multi-rater reliability testing.
